Layer 1 …Sawyer says allowance under review, hints at possible changes
The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) is considering an increase in its ₦20,000 monthly upkeep allowance for students amid concerns that rising living costs have reduced its purchasing power.
The Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on TVC’s Beyond the Headlines, saying the allowance was under constant review.
Although he did not announce a new amount or timeline for any adjustment, Sawyer confirmed that the possibility of an increase was being considered.
“Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said.
The proposed review comes amid complaints by students that the current allowance is inadequate to meet the rising costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic needs.
Sawyer, however, said any increase would have to take into account the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for all eligible beneficiaries.
“What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” he said.
Beyond the proposed review, the NELFUND chief disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was considering an intervention to provide students with more substantial financial support to help them complete their academic programmes.
He did not provide details of the proposed intervention, including its scope, funding or implementation timeline.
“I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” Sawyer said.
He also hinted that changes could be introduced in the future, although he gave no definite commitment on when the review would be concluded.
“I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added.
NELFUND’s proposed review comes as the Federal Government’s student loan scheme continues to expand, with millions of applications received from students seeking financial assistance for tertiary education.
According to figures provided by the fund, it has disbursed ₦180.5 billion in upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024, while another ₦194.7 billion has been paid to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees.
The combined disbursement of approximately ₦375.2 billion underscores the scale of the programme, which is intended to reduce financial barriers to tertiary education and help students remain in school.
The fund has also recorded more than 2.5 million applications and about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions.
Despite the programme’s expansion, the adequacy of the monthly upkeep allowance remains a concern for beneficiaries who depend on it to meet their daily expenses.
For now, the ₦20,000 monthly allowance remains unchanged, pending any formal announcement by NELFUND or the Federal Government on a possible increase or additional intervention.
